human_tolerance.notes: Prefers dense cover in forest, farm edges and suburban areas, nests readily in nest boxes, and is a familiar visitor at garden feeders in the northern part of its range.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Multiple broods during the summer breeding season; the female incubates a clutch of generally three to six eggs, creamy white with brown or reddish-brown spots and more heavily marked at the broad end. Cowbird parasitism peaks in April and is absent by July and August, which bounds the laying window.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Males sing to advertise territory year-round and at any point during the daytime except in the harshest weather; pairs hold the same territory for several years.

vocalizations.description: The ringing 'teakettle' song, rendered whee-udel, whee-udel, che-wortel, che-wortel and turtee-turtee, and familiar as 'sweet heart, sweet heart, come to me, come to me'. Sung by males only, year-round in any daytime weather short of the harshest, generally repeated three to five times though the male may repeat up to twelve.

Alarm calls, given by both males and females and the general response when a nest is threatened; the wrens judge a threat's size from its call, and a degraded call is taken to mean a distant intruder. Males alone also give a 'cheer' call in territorial disputes.

conservation.note: Wikipedia's speciesbox gives the IUCN 3.1 status least concern.

range.note: Permanent breeding locations run from eastern Nebraska, southern Michigan, southeast Ontario and New England south into Ontario, the northeast and southeast of Mexico and northern Central America; severe winters restrict the northern limits and mild winters extend the breeding range north.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia describes the bird spending its time on or near the ground, in tangles of vegetation and vines, probing bark crevices on lower tree levels, and picking up leaf litter; short hops and short flights between cover are the authored mapping of that movement, and it is rarely stationary when in the open.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia's breeding section is illustrated by a Carolina wren nesting in a duck nestbox; the species nests in enclosed sites rather than an open cup.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 18-23 g weight, which it notes is a fairly large wren.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives no typical lifespan and calls the species' lifespan relatively short. It reports the oldest female recaptured in Alabama at six years old and the oldest male at ten, against roughly 90 percent of banded southeastern wrens dying within 10 years; 6 years is the oldest female recapture and is the value used here.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia lists invertebrates as the diet (beetles, true bugs, grasshoppers, katydids, spiders, ants, bees and wasps), with small lizards and tree frogs making up the carnivorous portion, and says vegetable matter such as fruit pulp and various seeds makes up a small percentage. The 80/5 invertebrate-vertebrate and 10/5 seed-fruit split is authored judgement within the stated bounds, since no open source gives percentages.

traits.social.note: Genetically and socially monogamous, usually mating for life; after finding a mate, pairs maintain a territory and stay together for several years.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia states the wrens sing year-round and at any point during the daytime except in the harshest weather, and describes foraging through the day.

traits.defense.note: Wrens give alarm calls at the nest and attack intruders, judging a threat's size from its call and avoiding injury when attacking a large threat such as a blue jay; retreat into dense cover is the authored mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold and curious, energetically investigating a person in the open and readily visiting feeders, but shy of the open around the nest.

habitat.use.note: Wikipedia states the wrens spend the majority of their time on or near the ground searching for food or in tangles of vegetation and vines, and probe bark crevices on lower tree levels; the split between the two follows that description.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the leaf_litter entry follows Wikipedia's statement that the wren picks up leaf litter to search for prey, so it is recorded as cover rather than food; nesting and perch weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Preferred habitat is dense cover in forest, farm edges and suburban areas; Wikipedia records nesting in nest boxes and frequent use of bird feeders in the northern part of the range.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'These birds are largely resident, and will only disperse beyond their range after mild winters.'

seasonal.phases.note: Clutch size, egg description and female incubation are from the Breeding section, and the cowbird-parasitism figures (peaking in April, absent by July and August) bound the laying window; the month range itself is authored judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia gives no nestling period for this species; the 45-day juvenile duration and scale are authored judgement for a cavity-nesting wren.

vocalizations.note: Song descriptions, the male-only singing, the year-round daytime season, the three-to-twelve repetition range and the alarm/cheer calls are all from the Song and calls and Behaviour sections of Wikipedia; the cooldown is authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a rufous-brown upper body, buffy underparts, a bold white supercilium, and a long barred tail and barred wings. The eyebrow and tail-barring parts, the short cocked tail_ratio and the proportions are authored judgement to render the supercilium and barring the description names.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag is 'invertebrate' because the diet is predominantly insects and spiders taken from the ground and low vegetation, which also matches the program's ground foraging by hops; flee_m is judgement at a short radius for a bird that shelters in dense cover.
